faqs.a: At -100% the saturation multiplier becomes zero, so the color loses all chroma and turns into a neutral grey with the same lightness. It is a quick way to preview the greyscale version of any color.

The multiplier caps saturation at 100% of the HSL scale — a color that is already fully saturated cannot get more saturated, so +100% leaves it unchanged. On a muted color, +100% doubles its current saturation.
No — only saturation changes. Hue and lightness are preserved exactly, so a blue stays the same blue, just more or less vivid.

color-saturation-adjuster.formula:
new saturation = clamp(old saturation x (1 + amount/100), 0, 1)
hue and lightness are unchanged
amount ranges from -100% to +100%
howTo: Pick your base color or type its HEX code.
Move the slider left to desaturate (toward grey) or right to saturate (toward vivid).
Watch the before/after gradient and read the new HEX and HSL values.
Click Copy to place the result on your clipboard.
Use it in your CSS, presentation or design tool.
keyFacts: Saturation controls how vivid or muted a color looks.
The slider ranges from -100% (fully grey) to +100% (double saturation).
At 0% the color is completely unchanged.
Hue and lightness are preserved — only saturation moves.
Result saturation is clamped to the valid 0-100% HSL range.

limitations: Saturation caps at 100% — already-vivid colors cannot go further.
Only one color at a time; batch processing is not supported.
Very dark or very light colors show little visible change because HSL saturation has less effect near the extremes.
Works in HSL space, not perceptual LAB space.

Hue and lightness stay exactly the same — only saturation changes. The tool shows the new HEX and HSL values with a before/after preview, ready to copy into your designs.

color-saturation-adjuster.workedExample:
Take #4f46e5, which is hsl(243, 75%, 59%).
At -100%: new saturation = 0.75 x (1 - 1) = 0, so the result is hsl(243, 0%, 59%).
With zero saturation every channel equals the lightness: 0.59 x 255 = 150.45, rounds to 150.
Result: rgb(150, 150, 150) = #969696 — the exact grey version of the original color.
